shock.note: Two or more rises beyond the two-rise baseline means the Fed moved at every meeting or by a half point: inflation still accelerating into spring. One extra rise being priced between Jackson Hole and the September rise took the S&P down 1.2% (window). A second and third, with the 30-year mortgage already at 7.35% and equities at high multiples, does more than twice that; I put the S&P 5% below the baseline.
The 20+ year yield rose about 0.12 points while one extra rise was priced (window). Two or more extra rises with inflation not yet contained: 0.25 points.
The dollar proxy gained 1.5% over the window in which one extra rise was priced; two or more extra rises against a slowing Europe and Japan: 2.5%.

BND fell 1.7% over the window in which one extra rise was priced, more than its link to long yields gives, because 2- to 10-year yields carry the policy path. Roughly double that for two or more extra rises.

worst_outcome.title: The Fed's rate is 5.00% or higher after April: a rise at every meeting, or a half-point step
